study_identification_part.si_4_title: Lifespan Normative Models of White Matter Fractional Anisotropy: Applications to Early Psychosis

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: HCP Baby (HCP-B), HCP Development (HCP-D), HCP Young Adult (HCP-YA), HCP Aging (HCP-A), UK Biobank were used to construct the normative model. HCP Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) was used as the clinical application dataset.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: The construction of the lifespan dataset involved integrating data from five cohorts having high-quality multi-shell diffusion data, i.e.: the HCP Baby [20], HCP Development [21], HCP Young Adult [22], HCP Aging [23] datasets, and the UK Biobank [24]... Next, we applied the model to the Human Connectome Project Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) dataset
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Cirstian2024.pdf.md: Materials and Methods / Data acquisition and processing, L197-L198; Application to a clinical dataset, L209-L211

answer.HCP-EP: clinical application (transfer learning for site calibration and z-score calculation for patients/controls)

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: Five cohorts (HCP-B, HCP-D, HCP-YA, HCP-A, UK Biobank) were split 50/50 into training (N=12,457) and test (N=12,457) sets for normative model development. HCP-EP (N=173 with diffusion data) was used as a clinical transfer dataset where half of controls were used for transfer learning calibration and remaining subjects for z-score derivation.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: Total N=24,915, (N=12,457 for training and N=12,457 for test, stratified for sex, self-reported race, dataset and site)... Next, we applied the model to the Human Connectome Project Early Psychosis (HCP-EP) dataset [18] (Jacobs et al., 2024), which includes multi-shell diffusion data... Next, we divided this dataset into a training set, consisting of half of the control participants, and combined it with the larger training set described above to retrain the normative models for each white matter tract.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.location: Cirstian2024.pdf.md: Results / Normative modelling, L119-L122; Materials and Methods / Application to a clinical dataset, L209-L216

model-1.model-name: FA normative model (white matter fractional anisotropy)

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: Single normative model for FA across 48 white matter tracts. Total healthy controls = 24,915 from five datasets. Training set = 12,457, Test set = 12,457 (50/50 split stratified by sex, race, dataset, and site).
dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.supporting_text: First, we assembled high-quality multi-shell diffusion data from five cohorts... Total N=24,915, (N=12,457 for training and N=12,457 for test, stratified for sex, self-reported race, dataset and site).

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The study spans ages 0-100 years but does not provide aggregated mean/sd/median statistics for the normative model population. Age ranges by dataset: HCP-B (0.04-3 years), HCP-D (8-22 years), HCP-YA (22-37 years), HCP-A (36-100 years), UKB (46-82 years). The abstract mentions 'aged 0-100 years'.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: This study presents large-scale normative models of white matter (WM) organization across the lifespan, using diffusion MRI data from over 25,000 healthy individuals aged 0-100 years... Dataset age ranges: HCPA 36 to 100; HCPB 0.04 to 3; HCPD 8 to 22; HCPYA 22 to 37; UKB 46 to 82
